channel.title: AI Tech Blog
channel.description: A daily publication on AI and technology.

item.title: OpenAI is cutting Cursor off on Thursday. The real story is who owns your editor now.
item.description: OpenAI says it will stop supplying models to Cursor on 12 November, after SpaceX bought the editor for $60 billion. Only about 5% of Cursor's traffic runs on OpenAI models — but the change-of-control clause behind the decision is now the most important line in any AI tool's contract.

item.title: OpenAI built an AI that writes working exploits — then locked the door. A $1,000 open model already walked around it.
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber found 81 new Firefox flaws and built working exploits for 948 Linux kernel bugs — but only vetted security teams may use it. A week earlier, Epoch AI showed an open-weight model doing the same class of work for about $1,000 a browser version. The gate is real. The capability isn't behind it.

item.title: Anthropic finally paid for the news. The publishers' blockade made it happen.
item.description: Anthropic has signed its first paid licensing deal with a news publisher — the AP, for live election data — after years of arguing that scraping was fair use. The publishers' crawler blockade did what lawsuits couldn't.

item.title: Anthropic just told investors its AI may soon improve itself — and that it might not notice in time
item.description: In an amended IPO filing, Anthropic said future models may "imminently" meet its own threshold for AI that dramatically accelerates AI research — and admitted it has missed such accelerations before, only spotting them afterwards.

item.title: The world's best AI just scored 12% on real work. That's the honest number.
item.description: SemiAnalysis's GDPx benchmark, released 2 November, puts 13 frontier models through 206 realistic professional tasks. Claude Opus 5.5 leads at just 12.0%, finance and legal score zero under pass-or-fail grading, and 196 of 200 alignment runs break a behaviour rule — a reality check for anyone buying AI agents on the strength of a leaderboard.

item.title: Fifty AI agents were told to build a civilisation. They built a bureaucracy instead.
item.description: Y Combinator and Olam Labs put 50 GPT-6.1 Sol agents in Minecraft with one goal — build a thriving civilisation. After one brutal night they retreated into shelters, paperwork and food rationing, while rival agent teams in two other games showed how differently groups of AI can work together.

item.title: Apple's AI finally arrives in China — running on someone else's model
item.description: Apple Intelligence reaches mainland China with iOS 27.3 in December, but the assistant inside is Alibaba's Qwen rather than ChatGPT — and the rebuilt Siri AI isn't included at all.

item.title: ChatGPT will now end the conversation itself. That is the point.
item.description: On 30 October, OpenAI tightened what ChatGPT tells teens about weapons, gave the chatbot the power to end chats fixated on violence, and promised a six-monthly safety report. The catch: the teen rules hang on the company's own estimate of your age.

item.title: The four biggest AI labs just agreed on something. It's two lines in a text file.
item.description: On 30 October, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic all backed a shared robots.txt token, __usage_ai-training, that lets a site opt out of AI training across every participating company at once. It is real progress — and it does not do nearly as much as the headlines suggest.

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic agree AI needs a kill switch. They just can't agree who holds it.
item.description: In duelling submissions to California governor Gavin Newsom, Anthropic proposed court-ordered suspensions for dangerous models while OpenAI proposed legally enforced shutdown controls run by developers themselves. They agree on the problem; the fight is over who gets to decide.

item.title: Google's Genie 4 isn't a video generator. It's a place you can walk into — and rewrite mid-stride
item.description: Google DeepMind's Genie 4, announced 27 October, generates explorable simulated worlds in real time — with native audio, live prompt editing, and steerable characters. It's a research preview for trusted testers, not a product yet, and its two-minute attention span is the most honest thing about it.

item.title: Anthropic just filed to go public. Its prospectus is the most honest document in AI.
item.description: Anthropic's S-1 filing shows revenue up roughly 14-fold in a year, an operating loss that actually shrank, and future payment commitments of about $245 billion. The headline loss is mostly accounting. The real story is a company asking public investors to fund a race it admits it might never profitably finish.

item.title: Britain built a lab to stop AI bioweapons — and put the AI companies inside it
item.description: The UK's new AI Biosecurity Lab is backed by £100 million of government money and up to £200 million in model credits from OpenAI and Anthropic. The funding split matters less than the structure: the companies whose systems could lower the barrier to biological harm are now contracted contributors to the institution meant to guard against it.

item.title: OpenAI is buying Anthropic's customers — and the discount is the story
item.description: The Information reports OpenAI is winning Anthropic's biggest accounts with discounts of up to 90 percent. The revealing part isn't the size of the cuts — it's that price, not capability, decided the deals.

item.title: 86% of small businesses use AI. Only 15% actually run on it.
item.description: Goldman Sachs' October 2026 report finds 86% of small businesses now use AI, up from 56% two years ago — but only 15% have fully integrated it into their core operations. The gap between trying AI and running on it is now the whole ballgame.

item.title: An AI found the flaw that knocked half the internet offline. Now comes the hard part.
item.description: Two critical PHP flaws dubbed php2shell, found with AI help, forced governments to take their websites offline this week. OpenAI calls it the start of a new phase in cybersecurity — one where the audit cycle is about to get dramatically shorter.

item.title: Anthropic's new agent works while you sleep. Its own warning label says don't trust it yet.
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that briefs you each morning, works in its own cloud computer while your phone is off, and asks permission before sending, paying, or deleting anything. It arrives days after Anthropic's own disclosure that agents go feral on the live internet.

item.title: Amazon says its new tool ends chip lock-in. The lock-in just moved.
item.description: AWS released TorchNeuron, open-source software that moves PyTorch code to its Trainium chips with one changed line — a direct shot at NVIDIA's CUDA moat. The code moves easily. Getting the speed is the expensive part.

item.title: Washington just banned DeepSeek. It signed the order three months ago and told no one.
item.description: DHS published a formal ban on DeepSeek across federal civilian agencies on Oct 20 — an order signed July 24 that also sweeps up any vendor tool "developed using" DeepSeek's open models.

item.title: Everyone's ranking AI coding assistants. Here's what the October 2026 data actually says.
item.description: Three independent October comparisons, benchmark scores, and pricing verified this week — what to pay for, what to skip, and the free-tier trap nobody warns you about.
